Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(M_d=\max A_d\).

Taking \(i=j\) in the given condition gives
\[
|A_i|=i,
\]
so in particular \(M_i\ge i\) for every \(i\).

For any \(i,j\),
\[
|A_i\cup A_j|
=|A_i|+|A_j|-|A_i\cap A_j|
=i+j-\gcd(i,j).
\]
Since \(A_i\cup A_j\) is a set of positive integers, its maximum is at least its size. But
\[
\max(A_i\cup A_j)=\max(M_i,M_j),
\]
so
\[
\max(M_i,M_j)\ge i+j-\gcd(i,j). \tag{1}
\]

The positive divisors of \(250\) are
\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250.
\]
We use (1) on three pairs.

- For \(i=2,\ j=5\):
  \[
  \max(M_2,M_5)\ge 2+5-1=6.
  \]
  Since \(M_2\ge2\) and \(M_5\ge5\), this implies
  \[
  M_2+M_5\ge 8.
  \]

- For \(i=10,\ j=25\):
  \[
  \max(M_{10},M_{25})\ge 10+25-5=30.
  \]
  Since \(M_{10}\ge10\) and \(M_{25}\ge25\), this implies
  \[
  M_{10}+M_{25}\ge 40.
  \]

- For \(i=50,\ j=125\):
  \[
  \max(M_{50},M_{125})\ge 50+125-25=150.
  \]
  Since \(M_{50}\ge50\) and \(M_{125}\ge125\), this implies
  \[
  M_{50}+M_{125}\ge 200.
  \]

Also \(M_1\ge1\) and \(M_{250}\ge250\). Therefore
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250} M_d
\ge 1+8+40+200+250
=499.
\]

It remains to show that \(499\) is attainable.

For each positive integer \(d\), let \(B_d\) be a set of \(\varphi(d)\) positive integers, with all \(B_d\) pairwise disjoint. For the divisors of \(250\), choose them as follows:
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_1&=\{1\},\\
B_2&=\{2\},\\
B_5&=\{3,4,5,6\},\\
B_{10}&=\{7,8,9,10\},\\
B_{25}&=\{11,12,\dots,30\},\\
B_{50}&=\{31,32,\dots,50\},\\
B_{125}&=\{51,52,\dots,150\},\\
B_{250}&=\{151,152,\dots,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For all other \(d\), choose \(B_d\) to be any disjoint set of \(\varphi(d)\) unused positive integers.

Now define
\[
A_n=\bigcup_{d\mid n} B_d.
\]
Then
\[
|A_n|=\sum_{d\mid n}\varphi(d)=n,
\]
and
\[
A_i\cap A_j=\bigcup_{d\mid i,\ d\mid j}B_d
=\bigcup_{d\mid \gcd(i,j)}B_d
=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]
Hence
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=|A_{\gcd(i,j)}|=\gcd(i,j),
\]
so this sequence satisfies the required condition.

For the divisors of \(250\), we get
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d&1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\
\hline
M_d&1&2&6&10&30&50&150&250
\end{array}
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250} M_d
=1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250
=499.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
